subject: System Design
title: Double-Entry Bookkeeping
description: A short lesson to help you apply Double-Entry Bookkeeping.

hook.text: A $100 payment moves money from one account to another. Record it wrong and your books won't balance. Ever.

buildup.text: Double-entry bookkeeping records every transaction as two entries: a debit and a credit. They must always balance.

discovery.text: When you pay $100, one account is debited $100 and another is credited $100. The total always sums to zero.

twist.text: Modern payment systems use this 700-year-old accounting method in their databases — it's still the gold standard.

climax.text: Double-entry bookkeeping catches errors instantly. If debits don't equal credits, something went wrong.

punchline.text: Every debit has a credit — books must always balance.

quiz.question: Why is double-entry bookkeeping used in payment systems?
options: It catches errors instantly because debits and credits must balance
